chunks.text: Section 10 (Maharashtra Rent Control Act, 1999). (1) Save as otherwise provided in section 6, it shall not be lawful to claim or receive on account of rent, for any premises any increases above the standard rent and the permitted increases, unless the landlord was, before the coming into operation of this Act, entitled to recover such increase by virtue of, or under, the provisions of any of the repealed Acts or is entitled to recover such increase under the provisions of this Act. (2) Any contravention of provisions of sub-section (1) shall be an offence punishable, on conviction, with imprisonment not exceeding three months or fine not exceeding rupees five thousand or with both.

Section 11 (Maharashtra Rent Control Act, 1999). (1) After the commencement of this Act a landlord shall be entitled to make an increase of 4 per cent. per annum in the rent of the premises let for any of the purposes referred to in sub-section (1) of section 2. A landlord may also make reasonable increases for improvements or structural alterations made with the written consent of seventy per cent. of the tenants, and certain special additions, amenities, or heavy repairs as further provided in this section.

Section 14 (Maharashtra Rent Control Act, 1999). (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in any law for the time being in force and in the absence of an agreement to the contrary by the tenant, every landlord shall be bound to keep the premises in good and tenantable repair. (2) If the landlord neglects to make any repairs which he is bound to make under sub-section (1), within a reasonable time after a notice of fifteen days is served upon him by a tenant, such tenant may themselves make the same and deduct the expenses of such repairs from the rent or otherwise recover them from the landlord, subject to the limits in this section.

Section 15 (Maharashtra Rent Control Act, 1999). (1) A landlord shall not be entitled to the recovery of possession of any premises so long as the tenant pays, or is ready and willing to pay, the amount of the standard rent and permitted increases, if any, and observes and performs the other conditions of the tenancy, in so far as they are consistent with the provisions of this Act. (2) No suit for recovery of possession shall be instituted by a landlord against the tenant on the ground of non-payment of the standard rent or permitted increases due, until the expiration of ninety days next after notice in writing of the demand has been served upon the tenant. (3) No decree for eviction shall be passed on the ground of arrears if, within ninety days from service of summons, the tenant pays or tenders in court the standard rent and permitted increases then due together with simple interest at fifteen per cent. per annum, and thereafter continues to pay regularly till the suit is decided.

Section 16 (Maharashtra Rent Control Act, 1999). A landlord may recover possession if the court is satisfied of specified grounds, including that the tenant has unlawfully sub-let or given on licence the whole or part of the premises, erected a permanent structure without written consent, caused nuisance, ceased to use the premises for six months without reasonable cause, or that the premises are reasonably and bona fide required by the landlord for occupation by himself (subject to hardship safeguards). Unlawful sub-letting is an eviction ground under clause (e).

Section 26 (Maharashtra Rent Control Act, 1999). Notwithstanding anything contained in any law for the time being in force but subject to any contract to the contrary it shall not be lawful for any tenant to sub-let or give on licence the whole or any part of the premises let to him, or to assign or transfer in any other manner his interest therein: Provided that the State Government may by notification permit in any area the transfer of interest in premises held under such leases or class of leases other than those let for business, trade or storage to such extent as may be specified in the notification.

Section 29 (Maharashtra Rent Control Act, 1999). (1) No landlord, either himself or through any person acting or purporting to act on his behalf, shall, without just or sufficient cause, cut off or withhold any essential supply or service enjoyed by the tenant in respect of the premises let to him. (2) A tenant may apply to the court for a direction to restore such supply or service. The court may make an interim order directing restoration pending enquiry.

Section 31 (Maharashtra Rent Control Act, 1999). (1) Every landlord shall give a written receipt for any amount at the time when such amount is received by him in respect of any premises in such form and in such manner as may be prescribed. Failure to give a written receipt is punishable with fine for each day of default. This covers rent, deposits, and other amounts received in respect of the premises.

Section 24 (Maharashtra Rent Control Act, 1999). A licensee in possession of premises given on licence for residence shall deliver possession to the landlord on expiry of the period of licence. On failure, the landlord may recover possession by application to the Competent Authority. A licensee who continues after expiry may be liable to pay damages at double the rate of the licence fee fixed under the agreement.

chunks.instrument: Uttar Pradesh Regulation of Urban Premises Tenancy Act, 2021
chunks.text: Section 11 (UP Regulation of Urban Premises Tenancy Act, 2021; text aligned with Model Tenancy Act structure). (1) The security deposit to be paid by the tenant in advance shall be such as may be agreed upon between the landlord and the tenant in the tenancy agreement, which shall (a) not exceed two months rent, in case of residential premises; and (b) not exceed six months rent, in case of non-residential premises. (2) The security deposit shall be refunded to the tenant on the date of taking over vacant possession of the premises from the tenant, after making due deduction of any liability of the tenant.
chunks.notes: UP Act PDF from PRS is image-heavy; wording verified against Model Tenancy Act 2021 §11 which UP Act 16 of 2021 follows. Spot-check against gazette before production use.

chunks.instrument: Uttar Pradesh Regulation of Urban Premises Tenancy Act, 2021
chunks.text: Section 7 (UP Regulation of Urban Premises Tenancy Act, 2021; Model Tenancy-aligned). (1) After commencement, no tenant shall, except by entering into a supplementary agreement to the existing tenancy agreement, (a) sub-let whole or part of the premises held by him as a tenant; or (b) transfer or assign his rights in the tenancy agreement or any part thereof. (2) Where premises are sub-let upon such a supplementary agreement, the landlord and tenant shall jointly inform the Rent Authority about the sub-tenancy within two months from execution.
chunks.notes: Aligned with Model Tenancy Act 2021 §7; verify against UP gazette.

chunks.instrument: Uttar Pradesh Regulation of Urban Premises Tenancy Act, 2021
chunks.text: Section 21 (UP Regulation of Urban Premises Tenancy Act, 2021; Model Tenancy-aligned). (1) A tenant shall not be evicted during the continuance of the tenancy agreement unless otherwise agreed in writing, except in accordance with this section or related provisions. (2) The Rent Court may order eviction and recovery of possession on grounds including: failure to agree to pay rent payable; arrears of rent and other charges for two consecutive months not paid within one month of demand notice; parting with possession without written landlord consent; and continued misuse after notice to desist.
chunks.notes: Aligned with Model Tenancy Act 2021 §21; verify against UP gazette.

chunks.instrument: Uttar Pradesh Regulation of Urban Premises Tenancy Act, 2021
chunks.text: Section 20 (UP Regulation of Urban Premises Tenancy Act, 2021; Model Tenancy-aligned). No landlord or property manager shall, either by himself or through any other person, withhold any essential supply or service in the premises occupied by the tenant. On application by the tenant, the Rent Authority may pass an interim order directing restoration of essential services and may award compensation not exceeding two months rent after enquiry.
chunks.notes: Aligned with Model Tenancy Act 2021 §20; verify against UP gazette.

chunks.text: Section 11 (Model Tenancy Act, 2021). (1) The security deposit to be paid by the tenant in advance shall be such as may be agreed upon between the landlord and the tenant in the tenancy agreement, which shall (a) not exceed two months rent, in case of residential premises; and (b) not exceed six months rent, in case of non-residential premises. (2) The security deposit shall be refunded to the tenant on the date of taking over vacant possession of the premises from the tenant, after making due deduction of any liability of the tenant. This is a model for state adoption — not automatically binding in Maharashtra or UP unless enacted.

Section 31 (RERA Act, 2016). (1) Any aggrieved person may file a complaint with the Authority or the adjudicating officer, as the case may be, for any violation or contravention of the provisions of this Act or the rules and regulations made thereunder against any promoter, allottee or real estate agent. Explanation — For this sub-section, person includes the association of allottees or any voluntary consumer association registered under any law for the time being in force. RERA primarily covers real estate projects and promoter–allottee relationships; ordinary landlord–tenant rent disputes may fall outside RERA depending on facts. For Maharashtra RERA procedures see https://maharera.mahaonline.gov.in ; for UP see https://up-rera.in .

Section 19 (RERA Act, 2016) — Rights and duties of allottees. The allottee shall be entitled to obtain information relating to sanctioned plans and specifications approved by the competent authority; to know the stage-wise time schedule of completion of the project including water, sanitation, electricity and other amenities as agreed; and to claim possession of the apartment, plot or building as per the promoter's declaration. These rights apply in the promoter–allottee / real estate project context under RERA.
